mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate remains persistently below its long-run average for at least three consecutive months, it lowers real borrowing costs, encouraging risk-on sentiment and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05) during the low-rate period, or the three-month rate reversal does not coincide with a positive return window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in manufacturing production (INDPRO) signal weakening labor market strength, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor weakening events, or the combined index (PAYEMS - INDPRO) shows no significant negative correlation with SPX returns over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer spending (HOUST) coincident with a decline in industrial supply (INDPRO) suggests accelerating demand for goods relative to supply, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% while INDPRO decreases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant or are negative during such demand-supply events (two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, without a corresponding decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for three consecutive months and HOUST does not decrease by more than 2% in any of those months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of similar supply contraction episodes, or the supply shock is not detected in SPX via IC (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% triggers a one-month spike in risk aversion, reflected by a sharp rise in the S&P 500 20-day forward put premium and a negative return forecast over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during such UNRATE spikes, or put premium declines do not exceed historical averages.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceed expectations by more than 20% while inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3%, it signals a strong labor market that supports equity risk and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (consensus estimate + 20%) and CPIAUCSL < 300 for the same month
regime_hint: Strong labor demand with controlled inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such labor strength episodes, or the CPIAUCSL does not remain below 300.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail activity (HOUST) for two consecutive months, without a corresponding drop in consumer confidence proxies (not available), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to weakening demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of similar demand weakness episodes (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial supply (RSAFS) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand (HOUST) by at least 10% in the same month indicates a dual shock that tends to depress equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% while HOUST decreases by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such dual-shock events, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC < 0.10).
